Ryser's conjecture states that for any ''r-uniform'' and ''r-partite hypergraph'', <math>\tau(H) \leq (r-1)\cdot \nu(H)</math>. In the graph shown, which is 3-uniform and 3-partite, <math>3 \leq (3-1)\cdot 3</math> evaluates to <math>3 \leq 6</math>, so the conjecture holds.]]

In [[graph theory]], '''Ryser's conjecture''' is a conjecture relating the [[Maximum cardinality matching|maximum matching]] size and the minimum transversal size in [[hypergraph]]s.

This conjecture first appeared in 1971 in the Ph.D. thesis of J. R. Henderson, whose advisor was [[H. J. Ryser|Herbert John Ryser]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Lin|first=Bo|date=2014|title=Introduction to Ryser's Conjecture|url=https://math.berkeley.edu/~linbo/documents/CSS/RyserConjecture.pdf}}</ref>

== Preliminaries ==
A [[Matching in hypergraphs|'''matching''' in a hypergraph]] is a set of hyperedges such that each vertex appears in at most one of them. The largest size of a matching in a hypergraph ''H'' is denoted by <math>\nu(H)</math>.

A [[Vertex cover in hypergraphs|'''transversal''' (or '''vertex cover''') in a hypergraph]] is a set of vertices such that each hyperedge contains at least one of them. The smallest size of a transversal in a hypergraph ''H'' is denoted by <math>\tau(H)</math>.

For every ''H'', <math>\nu(H)\leq \tau(H)</math>, since every cover must contain at least one point from each edge in any matching.

If H is ''r''-uniform (each hyperedge has exactly ''r'' vertices), then  <math>\tau(H) \leq r\cdot \nu(H)</math>,  since the union of the edges from any maximal matching is a set of at most ''rv'' vertices that meets every edge.

== The conjecture ==
Ryser's conjecture is that, if H is not only ''r''-uniform but also ''r-partite'' (i.e., its vertices can be partitioned into ''r'' sets so that every edge contains exactly one element of each set), then:<blockquote><math>\tau(H) \leq (r-1)\cdot \nu(H)</math></blockquote>I.e., the multiplicative factor in the above inequality can be decreased by 1.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Ryser's conjecture {{!}} Open Problem Garden|url=http://www.openproblemgarden.org/op/rysers_conjecture|access-date=2020-07-14|website=www.openproblemgarden.org}}</ref>

== Extremal hypergraphs ==
An '''extremal hypergraph''' to Ryser's conjecture is a hypergraph in which the conjecture holds with equality, i.e., <math>\tau(H) = (r-1)\cdot \nu(H)</math>. The existence of such hypergraphs show that the factor ''r''-1 is the smallest possible.

An example of an extremal hypergraph is the [[truncated projective plane]] - the [[projective plane]] of order ''r''-1 in which one vertex and all lines containing it is removed.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Tuza|date=1983|title=Ryser's conjecture on transversals of r-partite hypergraphs|journal=Ars Combinatorica}}</ref> It is known to exist whenever ''r''-1 is the power of a prime integer.

There are other families of such extremal hypergraphs.<ref>{{cite arXiv|last1=Abu-Khazneh|first1=Ahmad|last2=Barát|first2=János|last3=Pokrovskiy|first3=Alexey|last4=Szabó|first4=Tibor|date=2018-07-12|title=A family of extremal hypergraphs for Ryser's conjecture|class=math.CO|eprint=1605.06361}}</ref>

== Special cases ==
In the case ''r''=2, the hypergraph becomes a [[bipartite graph]], and the conjecture becomes <math>\tau(H) \leq \nu(H)</math>. This is known to be true by [[Kőnig's theorem (graph theory)|Kőnig's theorem]].

In the case ''r''=3, the conjecture has been proved by [[Ron Aharoni]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Aharoni|first=Ron|date=2001-01-01|title=Ryser's Conjecture for Tripartite 3-Graphs|journal=Combinatorica|volume=21|issue=1|pages=1–4|doi=10.1007/s004930170001|s2cid=13307018|issn=0209-9683}}</ref> The proof uses the [[Hall-type theorems for hypergraphs|Aharoni-Haxell theorem]] for matching in hypergraphs.

In the cases ''r''=4 and ''r''=5, the following weaker version has been proved by [[Penny Haxell]] and Scott:<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Haxell|first1=P. E.|last2=Scott|first2=A. D.|date=2012-01-21|title=On Ryser's conjecture|journal=The Electronic Journal of Combinatorics|volume=19|issue=1|article-number=P23 |doi=10.37236/1175|issn=1077-8926|doi-access=free}}</ref> there exists some ε > 0 such that<blockquote><math>\tau(H) \leq (r-\varepsilon)\cdot \nu(H)</math>.</blockquote>Moreover, in the cases ''r''=4 and ''r''=5, Ryser's conjecture has been proved by Tuza (1978) in the special case <math>\nu(H)=1</math>, i.e.:<blockquote><math>\nu(H) = 1 \implies \tau(H)\leq r-1</math>.</blockquote>

== Fractional variants ==
A '''[[fractional matching]]''' in a hypergraph is an assignment of a weight to each hyperedge such that the sum of weights near each vertex is at most one. The largest size of a fractional matching in a hypergraph ''H'' is denoted by <math>\nu^*(H)</math>.

A '''fractional transversal''' in a hypergraph is an assignment of a weight to each vertex such that the sum of weights in each hyperedge is at least one. The smallest size of a fractional transversal in a hypergraph ''H'' is denoted by <math>\tau^*(H)</math>. [[Dual linear program|Linear programming duality]] implies that <math>\nu^*(H) = \tau^*(H)</math>.

[[Zoltán Füredi|Furedi]] has proved the following fractional version of Ryser's conjecture: If ''H'' is ''r''-partite and ''r''-regular (each vertex appears in exactly ''r'' hyperedges), then<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Füredi|first=Zoltán|date=1981-06-01|title=Maximum degree and fractional matchings in uniform hypergraphs|journal=Combinatorica|volume=1|issue=2|pages=155–162|doi=10.1007/bf02579271|s2cid=10530732|issn=0209-9683|citeseerx=10.1.1.115.2493}}</ref><blockquote><math>\tau^*(H) \leq (r-1)\cdot \nu(H)</math>.</blockquote>[[László Lovász|Lovasz]] has shown that<ref>{{Citation|last=Lovász|first=L.|chapter=Minimax theorems for hypergraphs|date=1974|title=Hypergraph Seminar|series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics|volume=411|pages=111–126|place=Berlin, Heidelberg|publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg|doi=10.1007/bfb0066186|isbn=978-3-540-06846-4}}</ref><blockquote><math>\tau(H) \leq \frac{r}{2}\cdot \nu^*(H)</math>.</blockquote>
